compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The review bot dequeues a review event and starts reviewing it immediately, without first
checking whether the revision that event describes is still the change's CURRENT revision. With
a single serial worker and reviews taking tens of minutes, a queued event is routinely obsolete
by the time it runs: the bot clones, reviews, and votes on a patchset the contributor already
replaced.

The queue should DISCARD a queued review before starting it when a newer patchset has been
pushed for that change.

## Mechanism

- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:218-247` — `_worker` does `event = await queue.get()` and then
  goes straight to `_voter.review_and_vote(event, ...)`. Nothing between the dequeue and the
  review re-reads the change's current revision. The event still carries the revision that was
  current when the webhook fired, which may be many minutes or hours earlier.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:80` — `WORKER_COUNT = 1`, with the rationale "One is enough for a
  single-box PoC (reviews serialize on the per-(change,rev) lock anyway)". That is what makes
  the staleness window large rather than theoretical: every review waits behind every other one.
- The capability to detect this ALREADY EXISTS but is not wired into this path:
  `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:258-275` — `get_change_event(change_id)` queries
  `/a/changes/{id}?o=CURRENT_REVISION` and shapes an event from the CURRENT revision. Its
  docstring scopes it to the manual `/rerun` path ("which has only a change id, not a live
  webhook payload"). The webhook path never consults it, so the one component that knows what
  "current" means is not asked.

## Observed evidence (2026-08-26, changes 2226/2231/2232)

The bot votes consistently ONE PATCHSET BEHIND:

    2226: PS6 uploaded 05:01:18 -> review bot voted on PS5 at 05:22:18   (superseded 21m earlier)
    2232: PS7 uploaded 05:59:01 -> review bot voted on PS6 at 06:10:12   (superseded 11m earlier)
    2232: PS8 uploaded 06:21:35 -> review bot voted on PS7 at 06:30:30   (superseded  9m earlier)

Each of those votes consumed a full LLM review of a tree that no longer existed.

## Impact

1. **Wasted spend and wall-clock.** Every stale review is a full clone + multi-pass LLM run
   against a superseded tree. On a single worker that time is not merely wasted, it is time the
   queue could not spend on current work.
2. **Contributors act on findings that are already fixed.** A `-1` arrives citing a defect the
   author corrected in the patchset the bot skipped. In this session that produced real churn:
   fixes were authored, and re-pushed, in response to superseded findings — which enqueued MORE
   reviews and deepened the backlog. The failure mode is self-amplifying.
3. **Head-of-line blocking for unrelated changes.** Because the worker is serial, stale reviews
   delay everyone. During this session changes 2225 and 2234 sat at `LLM-Review +0` for 90+
   minutes behind a queue whose head was doing obsolete work.

## Proposed fix

In `_worker`, between the dequeue and the review, read the change's current revision and drop
the event when it no longer matches — logging a countable marker in the same greppable style as
the existing `VOTER_ERROR` timeout path (`app.py:252-265`), so discards are observable rather
than silent.

Discarding is SAFE and does not lose the review: the newer patchset fired its own
`patchset-created` webhook, so an event for the current revision is already in the queue behind
this one. The change still gets reviewed — at the revision that actually exists. The existing
backfill reconciler (`reconcile.reconcile_once`, already the stated safety net for the abandoned
-on-timeout case) covers the residual risk of a genuinely lost event.

Design points the implementer should decide explicitly:

- **Cost:** one extra REST read per dequeue, against a 15-45 minute review. Negligible, but it
  should fail OPEN — if the current-revision read errors, review the event rather than dropping
  it, so a Gerrit blip cannot silently swallow reviews.
- **Force/rerun events** (`_rebar_force`, and `manual-rerun` from `get_change_event`) are built
  from the current revision by construction; they should bypass the check rather than race it.
- **Do not discard the newest event for a change** — only ones strictly superseded by a later
  revision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A queued review event whose revision is no longer the change's current revision is
      discarded BEFORE the clone/LLM work starts, not after.
- [ ] The discard is observable: a countable, greppable marker (sibling to the existing
      `VOTER_ERROR` timeout marker) naming the change and the superseded revision.
- [ ] An event for the CURRENT revision is still reviewed normally — the discard must not cause
      a change to go unreviewed.
- [ ] The staleness check fails OPEN: an error reading the current revision results in the
      review running, never in a silent drop.
- [ ] Force / manual-rerun events are not dropped by this check.
- [ ] Regression coverage: a queued event for revision N with the change now at revision N+1 is
      discarded; an event at the current revision is not.

## Verification

Every criterion above is proven by a named test in `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`. Run it with
the worktree interpreter — the `reviewbot` extra supplies fastapi, and WITHOUT it these tests
SKIP rather than fail, so a skipped run is NOT a pass:

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q -p no:randomly

Per-criterion proving tests:

| criterion | proving test |
|---|---|
| superseded revision discarded BEFORE the review | `test_worker_discards_a_superseded_revision_before_reviewing_it` |
| the discard emits a countable marker | same test — asserts a `_voter_error` marker was emitted |
| current revision still reviewed | `test_worker_reviews_the_current_revision` |
| unreadable current revision FAILS OPEN | `test_worker_fails_open_when_the_current_revision_cannot_be_read` |
| forced / manual rerun bypasses the check | `test_worker_does_not_discard_a_forced_rerun` |

Gates that must also pass:

    env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint
    env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck
    python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check

Proof the oracle has teeth rather than being a tautology: with the staleness check removed,
`test_worker_discards_a_superseded_revision_before_reviewing_it` must FAIL while the other three
still PASS. The first test proves the bug exists; the other three prove the fix did not
over-correct into dropping live work, failing closed on a Gerrit blip, or killing manual reruns.

file_impact.reason: Add the pre-review staleness check in _worker: drop a dequeued event whose revision is no longer the change current revision, fail-open, emit a countable marker
Regression coverage: superseded revision is discarded before review; current revision still reviewed; read error fails open; force/rerun bypasses

compiled_state.title: Review bot reviews superseded patchsets: the queue never re-checks current revision before starting a review
